notInitialized: This machine has not been initialized yet; run `peach init` first.

serve.mdnsLoopback: mDNS not published: --host {{host}} only allows local access, so publishing peach.local would point to an unreachable address. Use --host 0.0.0.0 for LAN access.
serve.noAuthNotLoopback:
Refusing to start: --no-auth is only allowed when listening on a local address, and --host {{host}} is not.
Turning off login on a LAN address hands the whole library and write APIs to any device on the network.
serve.noToken:
Refusing to start: --host {{host}} allows other devices, and this machine has no access token yet.
Started like this, any device on the network could read the whole library and call write APIs.
Run `peach token` to create and view the token (stored in {{path}}), then start again; for local use only, switch to --host 127.0.0.1.

token.lanHint: Services bound to a LAN address must be able to read it; view it with `peach token`.
token.relogin: Browsers that were signed in must sign in again; running services pick up this token after a restart.
token.shared: When two machines fetch each other's review results they send their own token, so the reader must use the same file as the writer.

blanks.header: These coordinates are empty (not an error; single-machine setups leave them empty):

blanks.writerOriginEffect: the reader does not mirror reviews

next.existing1: 1. Open the file above and check it, especially [media.mounts] and [replication].
next.existing2: 2. Restart the service to apply it. Until then nothing changes.
next.existing3: 3. Get the token with `peach token`: services bound to a LAN address won't start without it, and devices already in use must sign in again.
next.open: 2. Open http://127.0.0.1:{{port}}/ in a browser to confirm the page works.
next.lanLoopback: 3. For LAN access use --host 0.0.0.0 and install the local CA on each device. An access password is optional and set on the configuration page.
next.lan: 3. LAN devices need the local CA installed. An access password is optional and set on the configuration page.

sources.intro: Checking source pages and image CDNs; being reachable does not mean metadata or login sessions were verified.

help.mediaRead: Read a media directory and companion files with a time limit
help.init: First run: with no options, asks questions in the terminal; any option or --no-input runs non-interactively
help.noInput: Skip the questions and generate from options and built-in defaults
help.dataRoot: Peach data directory; defaults to the one currently discovered
help.fromExisting: Only create a settings file for a running deployment; create no directories or database
help.mdnsName: Name this machine publishes on the LAN (<name>.local)
help.writerOrigin: Writer origin the reader mirrors reviews from
help.writerProxy: HTTP proxy used only for the writer origin
help.sharedRoot: Shared transfer point for ledger replication
help.smbHost: Host of the shared transfer point
help.smbUser: Account used to mount the share
help.mount: Map a storage ID to a local media directory, e.g. local=/mnt/media; repeatable
help.setup: Serve only the first-run form: ignore the discovered Peach data directory and require no token
help.noAuth: Skip the login page; only allowed for local access, and never reads or changes the token file
help.scan: Scan the directories of one storage and save file details to the database
help.scanRoot: Media directory to scan; when omitted, uses the storage's configuration ([media.mounts] outside Windows)
help.process: Scan files and fill in library metadata
help.token: Show the LAN access token, creating one if needed
help.rotate: Replace the token; issued cookies stop working immediately
help.tunnel: Run or inspect the Cloudflare Tunnel (an access password must be set by default)
help.httpsPort: Actual HTTPS port of the source deployment (8443 on macOS, 443 elsewhere by default)
help.checkSources: After installing, run a bounded check of external metadata sources and image CDNs without reading videos
help.source: Check only this source ID; repeatable, defaults to all metadata sources
help.doctor: Diagnose configuration, database, tools and mounts item by item without repairing anything

server.description: Run the Peach service managed from the browser
server.accessIgnored: Access is already set up, ignoring {{env}}; change the access password in Settings under Network and access.
server.accessRejected: {{env}} was not used: {{error}}. Opening Peach in a browser leads to the access setup.
server.processFailed: Library processing failed with exit code {{code}}
server.updateTokenFailed: The one-click update token could not be created: {{error}}
server.listening: Peach is listening on {{host}}:{{port}}. Access from outside the container follows the host port mapping.
server.firstSetup: First-time setup: open Peach in a browser on the host or the LAN and follow the page.
server.firstOpen: First open: open Peach in a browser on the host or the LAN, then set an access password or turn off sign-in.
server.firstSignIn: First sign-in: run peach token where Peach runs to see the access token, then set an access password after signing in.
server.lanAccess: NAS / LAN access: set PEACH_BIND in Compose to the host's LAN IP; 127.0.0.1 allows only the host.

trayCommand.description: Start the Peach tray (the menu bar item on macOS) and manage services on this device; usually run without arguments.
trayCommand.silent: Show only the tray after starting
